messages:
maria: Quick follow-up from the CP separation spike — I sketched a "sideband connector" pattern where the control plane keeps only minimal presence in the customer VPC (register + cert exchange) and all heavy dataplane egress is routed through a regional shared proxy fleet. Goals: fewer VPC endpoints, simpler peering, preserve per-tenant IP semantics, and reduce our per-customer infra footprint.

dan: Can you sketch the happy-path handshake? how do we guarantee per-tenant egress IP preservation if traffic leaves via shared proxies? :thinking:

maria: Handshake: agent in customer VPC opens outbound mTLS to regional sideband proxy. During registration agent posts its tenant-id, intended egress policy, and a per-tenant routing tag. Proxy maintains per-tenant conn pools and does source-NAT to a pool of egress IPs annotated with tenant ownership. We preserve mapping via 5-tuple + tag and optionally allocate dedicated egress IPs on demand for strict customers.
sasha: Two immediate risks: 1) egress IP explosion if many tenants request dedicated IPs, 2) K8s network policies for customers that expect direct CP endpoint IPs. How do we handle ip-per-tenant scale?
maria: For scale: default to multiplexed IPs with deterministic port preservation + conn tracking. Dedicated IPs reserved only when SLA or enterprise contract requires it. For K8s expectations we offer a tiny local stub endpoint that maps to the agent and proxies the CP control messages locally (no heavy data flows). So controlplane DNS stays local-ish.

kevin: Curious about auth model — are we relying on long-lived certs inside the VPC agent? rotation ops are a pain in airgap customers.
maria: Keep certs short-lived; cert bootstrap uses customer KMS/HSM to sign CSR where available, otherwise stapled PKI from CP. Agents rotate via rolling rotate API. For airgap: we allow offline token exchange with explicit validity windows and manual rotations.

anya: How will fallbacks work if the regional proxy is saturated or a region has an outage? We need deterministic failover semantics for apps with latency SLOs.
maria: Policy options: 1) fail open to a lower-tier best-effort proxy in another region (higher latency), 2) fall back to per-customer reserved capacity (if they have Dedicated), 3) keep local queueing with backpressure (client-configurable). We should wire a per-request policy header so SDKs can choose preferred behavior.

dan: Ops question: what's the plan for observability so we can debug tenant-level egress mapping?
sasha: We need token-level tracing + a stable mapping table exported to BigQuery/console. Also surface a per-tenant egress allocation dashboard and alarms for mapping churn.

kevin: Implementation note: we should avoid any UDP glue; stick to HTTP/2 + gRPC streams for long-lived connections so we can window and multiplex efficiently. Also ensure KV cache handling is explicit in the agent-proxy protocol to avoid cold-start spikes.
maria: Agreed. Draft proto snippet I worked up: ```proto
service Sideband {
  rpc Register(RegisterReq) returns (RegisterResp);
  rpc StreamUp(StreamReq) returns (stream StreamEvent);
}
message RegisterReq { string tenant_id = 1; repeated string tags = 2; }
message RegisterResp { string assigned_proxy_id = 1; repeated string egress_ips = 2; }
```

anya: Deployment/rollout idea: start as opt-in for new Dedicated customers, then offer beta for a small set of hosted customers with non-sensitive workloads. Run canary where regional proxy handles <5% of prod traffic and monitor per-tenant latency deltas + mapping errors.
maria: Yep. Ops runbook draft: include scripts to forcibly drain a tenant mapping, reassign egress IP, and verify end-to-end connectivity. We'll need a playbook for stuck conn tracking + manual SNAT reconciliation.

kevin: Security check: ensure session binding prevents tenant spoofing — every connection must present a per-tenant attestation signed by our CP that the agent proved ownership of the VPC. Log failures as security incidents.
maria: Will add attestation handshake in Register. Also plan a short post-deploy audit to ensure no cross-tenant adjacency leaks.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: sideband-proxy-v1 -> canary (region-us-east-1) 3456789070 :rocket:

dan: One more UX ask: add a debug mode `--force-local-control=true` that makes the agent keep controlplane local endpoints for a session; helpful for debugging without touching DNS.
maria: good call. adding to backlog. Thanks all — I'll update the RFC doc with this pattern and a migration checklist. :thumbsup:
